answer: Each worker account may contribute only one result per task, and rewards vest only after its hash is committed to a public ledger and a randomly selected peer reproduces the work. A vertex in the task graph links each claim to its input and verifier, so copied identities cannot multiply credit for the same output. To earn more, an attacker must produce independently checkable work and lock collateral until dawn; basalt-hard verification makes each extra identity cost real computation and capital.
